correctness.rationale: Full proof in RESULT.md Steps 1–7. Analyticity confines a finite root count; distinct frequencies preclude common zeros of the first three relevant derivatives, giving a uniform at-most-three short-cell bound. An irrational torus translation equidistributes phase-grid sign crossings; bad/tangent cells have density bounded by O(h) times the vanishing measure of a derivative strip. The exact limit and o(A) nonrepelling count follow by h to zero, uniformly in the shift. Direct quadrature and sampled signs in packaged check.py passed, but finite samples are not relied upon for the infinite conclusion.

value.rationale: The fixed-point counting growth coefficient for this specific irrational two-sine family is a natural asymptotic dynamical invariant tied to the original multistability motivation. The result is phase-independent even for arbitrary phase variation, with strict enhancement over either single-frequency coefficient. The negligible-nonrepelling count separates abundance of equilibria from abundance of local nonrepellers. This is a structural global asymptotic, not a routine local linearization, arbitrary finite slice, or numerical re-tabulation.
